what: Cloud CRM for sales, service and marketing, with a customizable data platform.
mcpNotes: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers (developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/hosted-mcp-servers; GitHub forcedotcom/mcp-hosted) went GA on 2026-04-29, after a beta in October 2025. They cover standard servers (sObject operations, etc.) and custom servers, with per-user OAuth 2.0 + PKCE through an External Client App. Supported clients include Claude and ChatGPT. Available in Enterprise Edition and above, and included in Developer Edition. The docs say the servers are intended for Flex Credits customers and usage may be billed. There is also the open-source local Salesforce DX MCP server (forcedotcom/mcp).
blockerNotes: Developer Edition orgs are free and self-serve. To serve many customers, each org's admin must install or approve the External Client App, because ECAs don't exist in a target org until they are installed. Production orgs need an API-enabled edition (Professional Edition needs a paid add-on). Do not rely on the Username-Password flow, since ECAs don't support it. Event triggers come from Change Data Capture and Platform Events through the Pub/Sub API (gRPC) or CometD streaming, and from SOAP-based Outbound Messages. These are not simple JSON webhooks.

what: CRM platform for sales, marketing, service and CMS, with a broad public API.
mcpNotes: Remote server: https://mcp.hubspot.com. It uses OAuth 2.0 through a user-level app. It gives read and write access to CRM objects such as contacts, companies and deals, and read-only access to some other content. Custom sensitive-data properties are excluded. HubSpot also publishes a local Developer MCP server through the HubSpot CLI (`hs mcp setup`, requires Developer Platform 2025.2).
blockerNotes: OAuth app creation and testing are self-serve. A multi-tenant toolkit, however, is capped at 25 installs until it passes HubSpot Marketplace review and is listed. Listing also requires 3 active, unaffiliated installs and imposes AI-connector rules (user-level permissions or HubSpot's MCP Server).

what: Sales CRM for managing deals, contacts, leads, activities and pipelines.
mcpNotes: Pipedrive runs a hosted MCP server, announced on 2026-06-30. Users connect through OAuth, and it is available on all plans with plan-based token limits. It can read and write deals, contacts, organizations, leads and activities. Official connectors exist for Claude (in Claude's marketplace since Aug 2026) and ChatGPT, and other clients can connect through a custom MCP connection. Search snippets of Pipedrive's support article give the endpoint as https://mcp.pipedrive.ai/mcp, but the current version of that page and the feature page (pipedrive.com/en/features/mcp-server) do not show the URL. Community servers also exist.
blockerNotes: A developer can get a sandbox, build an OAuth app, switch it to live as a private app, and share the unlisted install link with any company without Marketplace review. Marketplace approval is needed only for a public listing. Minor caveats: sandbox pricing is not stated officially, and inactive sandboxes are deleted.

what: Flexible, data-driven CRM for records, lists, workflows and relationship intelligence.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.attio.com/mcp is hosted by Attio and uses OAuth login, with no API keys needed. It is included on every plan. The query-particle-sql tool is plan-gated (Ultra).
blockerNotes: API keys and OAuth apps are self-serve on the Free plan, so building and testing can start now. A multi-tenant OAuth app serving many users' workspaces goes past the 25-workspace limit for unpublished apps. That requires publishing to the Attio App Store, which involves an Attio team review (up to 1 week) and listing requirements.

what: Open-source CRM with a custom data model, REST/GraphQL APIs, webhooks and MCP.
mcpNotes: https://{your-workspace-url}/mcp, streamable-http, OAuth 2.1 or an API-key Bearer token. The URL is per workspace, so cloud and self-hosted instances each have their own. Community servers also exist (e.g. jezweb/twenty-mcp).
blockerNotes: Minor caveats. The base URL varies by workspace and deployment (api.twenty.com vs a self-hosted domain). The OpenAPI spec is generated per workspace at /rest/open-api/core and /rest/open-api/metadata rather than published statically. Cloud rate limits are low (50/min on Pro). Cloud needs a paid plan after the 30-day trial. A free self-hosted instance works for development. Webhooks are configured in the Settings UI and have no event filtering.

what: A customizable work-management and CRM platform built from apps, items, tasks and workflows.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.podio.com/mcp is hosted by Progress (Podio's vendor). It uses OAuth, works with default credentials or your own API key's client ID and secret, and exposes 22 read/write tools. It is in beta, "intended for evaluation and testing".
blockerNotes:
Nothing major blocks a build. Minor caveats:
- Rate limits are modest at 1,000 calls/hour on base plans, and only paid plans can buy add-ons for more.
- A few restricted operations need a support request.
- The vendor MCP server is in beta.
- Some legacy doc pages are stale or return 410.

what: Cloud CRM for managing leads, contacts, deals, sales pipelines and workflow automation.
mcpNotes: Zoho hosts four pre-built CRM MCP servers on zohomcp.in: Data Insights, Data Operations, Module Customization, and Workflow & Process Automation. One example is https://zoho-crm-data-operations-60065097786.zohomcp.in/mcp/<key>/message. Org-specific URLs are under Setup > Developer Hub > MCP for AI Agents. The servers use OAuth on first use and work with any MCP client; Zoho names Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and Windsurf. Zoho also has a broader Zoho MCP console. CData, Pipedream and Workato offer third-party servers.
blockerNotes: There is no real blocker. The main engineering concern is handling multiple data centers: the accounts and API domains vary by region, so the toolkit must find the user's domain from the token response. Free-edition orgs get only 5,000 credits per day. Org-level CRM sandboxes need Enterprise or Ultimate, but the free Developer Edition covers testing.

what: Sales CRM for SMBs with calling, email, SMS, sequences and pipelines.
mcpNotes: The URL is https://mcp.close.com/mcp, over Streamable HTTP. Auth is OAuth 2.0 with DCR, or an API key in the Close-API-Key header. Scopes are mcp.read, mcp.write_safe and mcp.write_destructive. I confirmed this on developer.close.com/mcp. The docs site also has its own docs MCP at developer.close.com/_mcp/server.
blockerNotes: The API is broad, the OpenAPI spec is public and building is self-serve. A free dev org is available on request, or you can use the 14-day trial. A public multi-tenant OAuth app needs Close's review before other organizations can authorize it.

what: CRM for Google Workspace users that manages leads, contacts, companies and opportunities.
mcpNotes: I found no official Copper MCP server: nothing on developer.copper.com and no Copper announcement. Third-party servers exist: StackOne (58 tools), Apideck, Activepieces, Zapier, Composio, Boomi, Scalekit, and community projects such as Cotlet's Copper CRM MCP server and one on Glama.
blockerNotes: Per-user API keys work for a prototype, but they need a paid or trial Copper account, reportedly on the Professional plan or higher. A proper multi-user OAuth app needs Copper to register it manually through partners@copper.com, and there is only one all-access scope. There is no dedicated sandbox, so testing uses trial accounts.

what: Intapp DealCloud: CRM and deal management platform for financial services firms.
mcpNotes: Intapp hosts the MCP server per tenant at https://[tenant].my.intapp.com/mcp/celeste/DealCloud (copied from Tools > MCP Servers). Auth is per-user OAuth with discovery. It needs a 'DealCloud with Celeste' license and the MCP Access capability, and write tools must be toggled on by an admin. Supported clients are Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot Studio and Cursor, plus some local clients once enabled. Clients not on that list need to contact their Account Manager.
blockerNotes: The docs are public, but every credential lives inside a licensed enterprise tenant. There is no free sandbox for DealCloud FS, and the UAT instance is paid. A toolkit could use per-customer client ID and API key auth against tenant URLs, but building and testing it needs a tenant from Intapp or a customer. Third-party MCP clients that aren't on Intapp's list need Account Manager approval. There are no push webhooks. Events come from polling Publication topics.

what: Customer support helpdesk suite: tickets, help center, messaging, AI agents.
mcpNotes: Zendesk hosts an official MCP server for each account, e.g. https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/mcp. It is offered under 'Zendesk Bridge / external AI agents' and is currently in an early access program (EAP) that customers must join. It authenticates with an OAuth client and is available on Suite Team and higher and Support Team and higher. The MCP Client, for calling external servers from action flows, is a separate product that is GA. Third-party servers also exist, from Pipedream, Swifteq and reminia, among others.
blockerNotes: Development on a free trial with a local OAuth client or API token is self-serve. Shipping a public multi-tenant toolkit needs a global OAuth client, which Zendesk must approve after a Marketplace-portal request from a d3v- sponsored account. Each user's subdomain must be collected.

what: Customer messaging, support inbox and helpdesk platform with Fin AI agent.
mcpNotes: US: https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp. EU: https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp. Each region also has a deprecated SSE endpoint at /sse. AU workspaces aren't supported yet. Auth is OAuth (recommended) or a bearer token. The Fin Operator tools need an OAuth connection and a workspace that has Fin Operator.
blockerNotes: Development and testing are fully self-serve through a free developer workspace. A public OAuth app that installs into end users' workspaces must pass Intercom's review first, whether listed or unlisted, and review can take up to 7 business days. Any later changes need re-approval. Until then the app works only for the developer's own team.

what: Cloud customer support helpdesk and ticketing platform from Freshworks.
mcpNotes: Freshworks hosts an official MCP server at https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp. It became generally available on September 10, 2026, authenticates with an API key only and does not work on custom domains. It is available on the Growth (25 actions/min, 1,200 actions/yr), Pro (50/min, 6,000/yr) and Enterprise (100/min, 12,000/yr) plans. It offers 37 tools covering tickets, conversations, contacts, agents, groups, companies and solutions. Community and commercial alternatives: effytech/freshdesk_mcp, Enreign/freshdeck-mcp, Workato and CData.
blockerNotes: The REST API is public and broad, with per-user API keys. Caveats: there is no OAuth, so users must paste a key and subdomain. There is no free tier with API access; the 14-day trial works for development, but lasting test access needs a paid plan. Rate limits are per account and depend on the plan. The sandbox is Enterprise-only. Webhooks can only be set up by an admin inside automation rules; there is no API to subscribe to them.

what: Shared inbox and customer communication platform for email, chat, SMS and other channels.
mcpNotes: The server is at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp and uses Streamable HTTP. It requires OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and does not support Dynamic Client Registration, so the client needs a client ID and secret from a Front developer app. Authorization is user-scoped, and any teammate can connect. Rate limits are 100, 200 and 300 tool calls per minute on Starter, Professional and Enterprise. The docs page has no beta/GA label and no launch date, so the earlier claims about an April 2026 beta and August 2026 GA are unverified. Docs: https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server
blockerNotes: Development can start with a free developer account. Offering the integration to all Front customers requires publishing through Front's partnership program, where Front tests the app, may review it, and can refuse it. Partner integrations must use OAuth. Only admins can authorize OAuth apps, which limits which end users can connect.

what: B2B support platform unifying Slack, Teams, email and chat with ticketing and AI agents.
mcpNotes: The hosted server is at https://mcp.usepylon.com (US) and https://mcp.eu.usepylon.com (EU). It accepts OAuth, where you sign in to Pylon and requests run as you, or a Bearer API token. An admin enables it under Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server. The connecting identity needs the MCP Access permission. Some tool groups depend on plan features such as Feature Requests, Account Intelligence and custom analytics.
blockerNotes: The API is public, well documented and broad, and has an OpenAPI spec. The obstacles are getting a workspace and handling auth. Pylon has no free plan or self-serve trial, so a test workspace means a sales-arranged trial or a paid per-seat annual plan. The REST API has no third-party OAuth, so each customer's admin must hand over a non-expiring, role-bound token. MCP OAuth is an alternative for per-user auth.

what: Multichannel helpdesk and live chat software with ticketing, call center and knowledge base.
mcpNotes: Each account has its own built-in endpoint at https://<your-liveagent-domain>/api/mcp over Streamable HTTP. Auth is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE or a bearer token. The pricing page limits external MCP connections to the Business and Enterprise plans. I could not confirm the "early preview" label on the support article. QualityUnit, the vendor, also publishes a self-hosted Python server at github.com/QualityUnit/liveagent-mcp-server. It is small (7 commits) and uses LIVEAGENT_BASE_URL and LIVEAGENT_V3_API_KEY.
blockerNotes: The API needs a paid plan after the 30-day trial. Starter allows only 1 API key, and external MCP needs Business or higher. Credentials are per account and per domain, so users must enter their own subdomain and API key. The full API reference is only visible inside a logged-in account, though the OpenAPI descriptor and the generated SDK help. Outbound events need a Rules action that each user sets up in the UI ("HTTP request to external URL"). There is no API-managed webhook subscription.

what: API-first B2B customer support platform with AI agents and Slack/email/in-app channels.
mcpNotes: Vendor-hosted at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp. It uses OAuth ("No API keys needed") and has the same permissions as the Plain user. The docs say "nearly 400 tools".
blockerNotes: There is no free tier. Testing needs a 7-day trial (no credit card) or a paid workspace. OAuth apps only work in the workspace that created them, so no shared multi-tenant OAuth app is possible and the toolkit must rely on per-workspace API keys. The API is GraphQL only, with no OpenAPI spec.

what: Shared-inbox customer support platform with email, chat, Docs knowledge base and reports.
mcpNotes: Help Scout's official connector is at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp. Each user signs in with OAuth on Help Scout's own login page, and the connector registers itself, so a client ID and secret are optional. A Docs API key is optional and only needed for Docs tools. The article names Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor as clients. The connector is available on Standard, Plus and Pro, and its report tools need Plus or Pro. A community server also exists (drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server), but I did not re-verify it.
blockerNotes: The Free plan has no API access, so end users need Standard, Plus or Pro. For development, a 15-day Standard or Plus trial with no credit card appears to work. The docs describe no separate sandbox and no app review for OAuth apps. Help Scout publishes no official OpenAPI spec; only third-party specs exist (for example, Jentic).

what: Ecommerce-focused customer support helpdesk with tickets, macros, rules and AI agent.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.gorgias.com/mcp. Open beta, authorized in the browser by entering your subdomain and approving access. One Gorgias account per connection; for multiple brands, add a gorgias_subdomain parameter. Works on any plan at no extra cost. Reads are fully live, while some writes, such as Macro edits and AI Agent configuration, are restricted during the beta.
blockerNotes: Distributing to many merchants needs a public OAuth2 app, and that needs tech-partner review. A developer sandbox needs a draft app and partner-team approval. Without one, the only self-serve options are the 7-day trial or a paid plan from $10/month. Webhooks are outbound HTTP integrations that fire on ticket events, carry no signature, and are configured per account.

what: AI customer service platform that organizes support conversations around people, not tickets.
mcpNotes: I found no official Gladly MCP server. Gladly's site, developer docs and search results show no first-party announcement. Third-party hosted servers exist from StackOne (https://www.stackone.com/connectors/gladly/mcp/) and Truto.
blockerNotes: The API is broad, documented and has an OpenAPI spec, so a toolkit is technically simple. It would use Basic auth with the org subdomain, agent email and API token. However, there is no free or trial account, and getting a Gladly organization or sandbox to build and test against requires going through Gladly sales or a partnership. There is no OAuth either, so end users must paste unscoped, full-access tokens. Customers who already use Gladly could connect their own tokens.

what: Team chat platform with channels, DMs, files, canvases, and workflows.
mcpNotes: The server is at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp and uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP. SSE and Dynamic Client Registration are not supported. Auth is confidential OAuth with client ID and secret, with PKCE for desktop clients. Only Marketplace-published and internal apps can use it; unlisted apps are prohibited.
blockerNotes: A self-serve OAuth app can be built today with a broad Web API and the Events API. However, a commercially distributed app outside the Marketplace gets 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history and conversations.replies. That cripples message-reading tools. Using the official MCP server also requires Marketplace listing. To work at full capacity in production, the app needs Marketplace review.

what: Cloud communications APIs for SMS, voice, WhatsApp, email, video and verification.
mcpNotes: Twilio hosts an official MCP server at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs, in Public Beta since May 2026. It only searches and retrieves documentation through two tools, twilio__search and twilio__retrieve. It takes no credentials and cannot call any APIs. Twilio lists OAuth-authenticated MCP tools that execute API calls as a future item ("What's next"). For actual API calls, Twilio publishes the local package @twilio-alpha/mcp (github.com/twilio-labs/mcp), labeled "Twilio Alpha". It runs through npx and authenticates with an Account SID plus an API key and secret, and its README calls it one of "our official" servers.
blockerNotes: The API is public and documented, and credentials are self-serve. The caveats: trial accounts expire after 30 days and can only send to verified numbers. Real traffic needs a paid pay-as-you-go account plus regulatory work such as A2P 10DLC registration, which itself requires a paid account. Test credentials work on only 4 endpoints: buying phone numbers, sending messages, placing calls and Lookup; any other endpoint returns 403. Multi-user auth means collecting per-account API keys, or OAuth client credentials, which the user also has to set up.

what: Zoho's team chat app with channels, threads, calls, bots and extensions.
mcpNotes: Zoho documents a Zoho Cliq MCP Server (zoho.com/cliq/help/platform/zoho-cliq-mcp.html). It is provisioned through the hosted Zoho MCP console at mcp.zoho.com (zoho.com/mcp), which generates a remote MCP URL. Zoho's MCP setup page says you need "the appropriate plan" for the AI agent. I could not confirm the exact auth model or plan tiers from the pages I fetched.
blockerNotes: The REST API is broad, OAuth2 is self-serve, and a Free plan exists. Watch for three things: routing calls to the right data-center domain, the per-endpoint per-minute throttles, and the admin-only APIs. Triggers are weak because there are no native outbound event webhooks. Event handling lives in Cliq's own Deluge-based bot and extension handlers.

what: ByteDance's international workplace suite: chat, docs, calendar, base, approvals, and a developer open platform.
mcpNotes: The npm package is @larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp (github.com/larksuite/lark-openapi-mcp). It is in Beta and self-hosted, using stdio or SSE/HTTP. The --domain flag targets Lark international, and OAuth with --token-mode user_access_token is supported. Neither the repo nor searches showed a Lark-hosted remote MCP URL.
blockerNotes: The API is public, and creating a custom app on a free tenant is self-serve. A single OAuth app serving many external tenants must be published as a store app. That requires a Lark Open Platform listing review, and each tenant admin must also approve the install and its scopes. Lark international (open.larksuite.com) and Feishu (open.feishu.cn) are separate platforms with separate domains.

what: CAKE.com team chat app with channels, DMs, calls and third-party apps.
mcpNotes: The official remote MCP server is at https://mcp.pumble.com/mcp. CAKE.com announced it on 2026-07-01 as "available to all new and existing Pumble users." It authenticates with token and x-app-token headers from an app the user creates; the docs show no OAuth for it. The tools available depend on the scopes granted. There is also a Claude connector under Configure apps. Community servers exist too, such as the pumble-mcp-server npm package (shoutkol) and @infralayers/pumble-mcp.
blockerNotes: OAuth, scopes and event subscriptions (signed HTTP event delivery) are documented, and a developer can build and test for free. The catch is reaching arbitrary customer workspaces: that needs a Public app on the CAKE.com Marketplace, which goes through review, and each new version is re-reviewed. Private apps only work in whitelisted workspaces. Free-plan workspaces can install only 3 apps or integrations. Developer docs are mainly on the SDK site, cake-com.github.io/pumble-node-sdk.

what: Community chat platform; API for bots, messaging, guilds, and OAuth2 user integrations.
mcpNotes: Discord hosts a docs-only MCP endpoint at https://docs.discord.com/mcp. It is a Mintlify-style server that searches and retrieves developer docs and has a feedback tool. A GET returns HTTP 405, which fits a POST-only MCP endpoint. It does not wrap the Discord API, so it is not counted as an official product MCP. Product MCP servers are community-built, e.g. SaseQ/discord-mcp, which uses a bot token, plus Workato and other vendor connectors.
blockerNotes: The API is open and free but bot-centric. OAuth2 does not give user-level message read/send, so the toolkit acts as a bot that each user must install in their guild. Scaling past 100 guilds requires bot verification, and the MESSAGE_CONTENT, GUILD_MEMBERS and GUILD_PRESENCES intents then need approval. Some scopes, such as dm_channels.read, are partner-only. HTTP webhook events cover only app authorization, entitlements, and lobby/game DMs. Message and guild triggers need a persistent Gateway websocket connection.

what: Messaging platform with an HTTP Bot API and MTProto user-client API.
mcpNotes: No official Telegram MCP server was found. Community MTProto/user-account servers: chigwell/telegram-mcp (Telethon), sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram, overpod/mcp-telegram (GramJS), lexfrei/mcp-tg (Go), l1v0n1/telegram-mcp-server. There are also community Bot API-token servers.
blockerNotes: There is no delegated OAuth for API access. OIDC login gives identity and bot-DM permission only. Bots see only chats where they were started or added, or the chats a Business user explicitly connects (Premium only). Acting as a user requires an MTProto phone or QR login with ban monitoring and ToS risk. In a multi-user toolkit, each user would supply their own bot token.

what: Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API for sending/receiving business messages, templates and calls.
mcpNotes: Meta's official WhatsApp Business Tools MCP is at https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools (Streamable HTTP). It signs in with OAuth through a Meta developer account, using automatic client registration, so you don't need a client ID or a Meta app. It is in beta and rolling out gradually. It is built for development and testing (setting up accounts, phone numbers, templates, webhooks and test messages), not for production sending at scale. Requests are rate-limited per user per tool. Supported clients are Claude Code, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT and Codex. A separate Meta Business Messaging MCP is also rolling out.
blockerNotes: Building and testing is self-serve, with Standard Access and a test number. Letting arbitrary end-users connect their own WABAs needs Advanced access through Meta App Review, plus Tech Provider / Embedded Signup onboarding. Messaging is billed per delivered message after the free service-message tier. Template rules and the 24-hour customer service window limit what an agent can send.

what: Cloud phone/contact-center system for business calls, SMS and AI voice agents.
mcpNotes: No official Aircall-hosted MCP server. The developer MCP FAQ (last updated 2026-09-04) still says "we don't offer an MCP servier but stay tuned." The Sept 2026 blog post describes the reverse direction: partners register their own MCP servers so Aircall's AI agents can call them ("Register a Public MCP" / AI Actions). Third-party servers exist: themobilefirstco/Allo, itaygadot111, StackOne, Zapier, Composio, Metorial and Activepieces.
blockerNotes: Public multi-tenant OAuth needs Aircall Technology Partner approval (application, then integration-plan review, then OAuth apps issued). Without it, each end user must supply their own api_id/api_token from a paid Aircall account (or a trial). That works today but is clunky.

what: Cloud communications APIs: SMS, voice, messaging, verify, video, numbers.
mcpNotes:
Vonage publishes two official MCP servers:
- **Server API Bindings (Tooling) MCP server:** npm `@vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings`. It runs locally over stdio via npx and needs VONAGE_API_KEY/SECRET, APPLICATION_ID and PRIVATE_KEY64 set as environment variables. This is the one that can call the APIs.
- **Documentation MCP server:** hosted remotely at https://documentation-mcp.vonage.dev/mcp (HTTP). It only serves documentation and cannot call any APIs.
blockerNotes: There is no OAuth2, so users must paste an API key/secret or an application ID plus private key for JWT. Real sending beyond whitelisted test numbers requires topping up the account with credit, and trial credit is small. A free Messages API Sandbox (WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger, Instagram) helps with testing.

what: API for managing Google Ads campaigns, accounts, and reporting programmatically.
mcpNotes: The official server is google-ads-mcp (github.com/googleads/google-ads-mcp), installed with 'pipx install google-ads-mcp'; the docs pin 0.0.6. It runs locally over stdio with ADC (an OAuth client secret or a service account). You can also deploy it yourself on Cloud Run with streamable-http, which needs an OAuth web client. Google documents no hosted remote URL. The tools mainly read data (list customers, GAQL search, metadata). Writes are limited to assets, video uploads and labels; the server cannot change campaigns, ad groups, ads, budgets or bids. Third-party hosted servers exist (AdPlug, Sprites).
blockerNotes: There are two separate reviews. First, the developer token must reach Explorer, Basic or Standard access to reach production accounts. Explorer is usually automated, Basic needs brand verification, and Standard is reviewed manually. Second, Google OAuth app verification is needed because the Ads scope is restricted. There are no webhooks, so triggers would need polling. Operation quotas also depend on the access level.

what: Meta's Marketing API and hosted MCP server for managing and reporting on Facebook/Instagram ads.
mcpNotes: Meta-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.facebook.com/ads, announced on the Meta developers blog on 2026-07-16. Its tool categories are reporting, ad creation/management, catalogs, signals/datasets, help and troubleshooting, A/B tests and conversion lift studies, and activity logs. Auth is OAuth (Facebook Login for Business), a user access token, or a system user token. Owning a Meta app is not required. If you use your own app, you pass the app ID as the OAuth client ID and must match the redirect URL. The community server pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp also exists.
blockerNotes: A multi-tenant toolkit that serves other users' ad accounts needs Advanced access to ads_read/ads_management through App Review, and likely Business Verification. Development against your own accounts, or against a sandbox ad account, works immediately at Limited access. The getting-started page for the hosted MCP doesn't mention App Review. Meta's MCP blog says Advanced Access for your own app is requested under Permissions and features, then App Review.

what: LinkedIn Marketing API for managing ad accounts, campaigns, creatives, targeting, and reporting.
mcpNotes: I found no MCP server published by LinkedIn or Microsoft. Third-party servers include the PyPI package linkedin-ads-mcp (its page says "There's no official LinkedIn MCP"), the npm packages mcp-linkedin-ads and @cesteral/linkedin-mcp, AdKit, AdPlug, and Cequence AI Gateway.
blockerNotes: The app needs Advertising API approval. In the Development tier, edits are limited to 5 mapped ad accounts. Before arbitrary users can connect for writes, LinkedIn must grant a Standard tier upgrade through a support ticket, at its own discretion. Reads are unlimited in the Development tier. Lead webhooks need a separate Lead Sync API approval.

what: All-in-one CRM, marketing automation and white-label agency platform for agencies and SMBs.
mcpNotes: Vendor-hosted at https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/mcp/anthropic/v2 for Claude. Other clients have their own paths: /mcp/openai/v2/, /mcp/cursor/v2 and /mcp/muse/v2/. The server has 4 meta-tools (list_locations, search_operations, describe_operation, execute_operation) that reach 717 actions. Users sign in with their HighLevel login, with no API key.
blockerNotes: A toolkit used by many agencies needs a public Marketplace OAuth app, and public listing requires review and approval, including a Loom demo and justification for each requested scope. Development and testing are self-serve through a private app plus a sandbox account, which lasts up to 6 months. End users need a paid HighLevel plan, and some endpoints require the Founder plan.

what: Email marketing platform: audiences, campaigns, automations, ecommerce; Mandrill for transactional email.
mcpNotes: Two vendor-hosted MCP servers are documented, but neither gives access to Marketing account data. (1) https://mailchimp.com/developer/_mcp/server searches documentation only and needs no auth. (2) https://mandrillapp.com/mcp is the Transactional MCP, authenticated with a Bearer Mandrill API key. Mailchimp also ships a first-party Claude connector: the help article says to "Sign in with your Intuit Mailchimp account" from Claude's Connectors list. A ChatGPT app also exists. The hosted endpoint ai-inc.mailchimp.com/claude/mcp/v2 appears only in third-party directories. Mailchimp's docs do not document it as open to arbitrary MCP clients. Community servers (mailchimp-mcp, mcp-mailchimp, damientilman/mailchimp-mcp-server) use an API key.
blockerNotes: The REST API is broad, with an OpenAPI spec, self-serve OAuth registration, and no documented review. The 10-connection-per-user cap matters for heavy concurrent agent use.

what: Marketing automation platform for email, SMS and customer data/CDP.
mcpNotes: Official remote server at https://mcp.klaviyo.com/mcp. It uses OAuth with dynamic client registration and is limited to the Owner, Admin and Manager roles. Klaviyo also documents a local server option.
blockerNotes: The REST API, OAuth (PKCE) and a free account and test account are all self-serve. Marketplace listing needs review but is not required, because apps can be distributed by installation URL. Managing webhook subscriptions through the API is limited to Advanced KDP customers and app partners. Klaviyo also runs an official remote MCP server.

what: All-in-one funnel builder, email marketing, courses and e-commerce platform.
mcpNotes: Official remote server at https://mcp.systeme.io/mcp?mcpKey=YOURMCPKEY. The MCP key goes in the X-MCP-Key header or the mcpKey query parameter. The server is an initial release covering contacts, tags, contact fields and newsletters only. All MCP keys share one rate-limit quota. A community local server also exists (snzeeee/mcp-server-systeemio).
blockerNotes: There is no OAuth, so authentication uses a per-user API key (3 keys per account). Webhooks can be registered through the API (POST /api/webhooks) for six events: CONTACT_OPT_IN, CONTACT_CREATED, CONTACT_TAG_ADDED, CONTACT_TAG_REMOVED, SALE_NEW and SALE_CANCELED. Rate limits vary by plan.

what: Visual discovery platform; API for pins, boards, ads, analytics and catalogs.
mcpNotes: developers.pinterest.com/about-pinterest-mcp/ shows https://api.pinterest.com/mcp (http transport, Bearer token, OAuth 2.0) in an example config. On re-check the page is still a pre-launch announcement ("Be the first to know when it launches", "Sign up for updates"), so the server is announced but not confirmed live. Several community MCP servers also exist.
blockerNotes: Pinterest must approve the app before it gets Trial access. Trial content lives in a creator-only sandbox and has daily per-app rate limits. A multi-user production toolkit needs the Standard upgrade, which is reviewed and requires a video demo of the OAuth flow. Webhooks exist only for lead ads.

what: Meta's Threads API: publish posts, read profiles/replies, moderate, get insights.
mcpNotes: Only community servers exist, for example the PyPI packages mcp-threads and meta-threads-mcp (which describes itself as 'Unofficial') and the GitHub repos pegasusheavy/threads-mcp (Pegasus Heavy Industries LLC) and baguskto/threads-mcp. No MCP server from Meta was found.
blockerNotes: Development and testing work with free self-serve credentials and invited Threads Testers. Public multi-user use needs App Review for each permission and a published app. Advanced Access, which webhooks need for tech providers, also needs Business Verification. Tokens last 60 days and must be refreshed.

what: Twilio SendGrid: cloud email API for transactional and marketing email.
mcpNotes: I found no official Twilio SendGrid MCP server. Twilio's blog post 'Build a SendGrid MCP Server' is a community contributor tutorial whose code lives in the third-party repo FINCH285/SendGrid-MCP-Server. Community servers include neschadin/sendgrid-mcp, Garoth/sendgrid-mcp, deyikong/sendgrid-mcp and @codespar/mcp-sendgrid, plus hosted options from Pipedream, Composio and Metorial. Twilio's own MCP server (twilio-labs/mcp) is reported to cover the Twilio Public API, not SendGrid v3; I saw that only in a secondary source.
blockerNotes: Per-user API keys are self-serve, and there is no OAuth app review. Caveats: new accounts get only a 60-day, 100 emails/day trial before a paid plan is needed, and senders must verify a sender identity or domain. Twilio's docs have a page on Sandbox Mode for mail send over Web API v3.

what: Ecommerce platform for online stores, with APIs for products, orders, customers and checkout.
mcpNotes: Shopify's official Dev MCP server is the @shopify/dev-mcp package (npx -y @shopify/dev-mcp@latest). It runs locally without authentication and gives access to developer docs and API schemas. It is part of the Shopify AI Toolkit, which can also run supported store-management tasks through the authenticated store context of the Shopify CLI. That path is local and CLI-based; it is not a hosted multi-tenant admin MCP. I found no vendor-hosted remote MCP for admin operations on shopify.dev. Third-party blogs mention an @shopify/admin-mcp package, but it is unverified. The first pass described shopper-facing Storefront, UCP and Checkout MCP endpoints, and I did not re-verify those in this pass.
blockerNotes: Development and testing are free on development stores. A multi-merchant OAuth app needs public distribution, which requires Shopify approval and paid App Store registration (a one-time fee). Tokens are per shop. New public apps must use the GraphQL Admin API, and there is no OpenAPI spec.

what: Open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin with a REST API for store data.
mcpNotes: Developer preview. WooCommerce registers purpose-built abilities through the WordPress Abilities API, for example woocommerce/products-query and woocommerce/order-notes-query. They cover querying, creating, updating and deleting products, querying orders and order notes, updating order status, and adding order notes. The WordPress MCP Adapter plugin exposes them on each store at /wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server. Local sites can connect over WP-CLI STDIO. Remote sites connect through the @automattic/mcp-wordpress-remote proxy with an Application Password. There is no vendor-hosted URL. WooCommerce 11.3 removed the old /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint and the older REST-derived abilities, such as woocommerce/products-list.
blockerNotes: The API is open and free, but every store is self-hosted. Each user must supply a store URL and either create keys by hand or approve the /wc-auth/v1/authorize flow. There is no central OAuth2 app and no official OpenAPI spec. Some hosts strip Authorization headers or lack HTTPS. A test store is self-provided: anyone can spin up a free local WordPress and WooCommerce install.

what: Hosted ecommerce platform: storefronts, catalog, orders, customers, with headless APIs.
mcpNotes: Store Management MCP is at https://api.bigcommerce.com/mcp, with a store-scoped URL that includes the store hash. It is in early access for all stores, uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, and only the store owner can enable it. Storefront MCP gives each storefront its own URL and acts as a shopper; the store owner enables it. Community servers also exist.
blockerNotes: A multi-merchant OAuth toolkit needs BigCommerce approval before stores outside the developer's own email can install the app, whether it is listed or unlisted. Until then, the options are draft-app installs on the developer's own stores, or each merchant pasting a store-level API token. Both are workable as a fallback but don't scale like OAuth.

what: Salesforce B2C Commerce Cloud: enterprise ecommerce platform with Shopper and Admin REST APIs (SCAPI).
mcpNotes: Official local server: npm package @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp, run with npx -y @salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp@latest. Salesforce's PWA Kit docs title it 'B2C DX MCP Server (Developer Preview)'. It is developer-focused: docs search, cartridge/MRT deploy, debugging, WebDAV, CIP analytics, and SCAPI Admin and Shopper calls (~600 operations). Salesforce also offers a vendor-hosted B2C Commerce MCP Shopper Service (SSE, SLAS tokens) that is pilot-only, with access through your Salesforce account executive. Community servers exist (e.g. sfcc-dev-mcp, Cequence AI gateway).
blockerNotes: The API is public, well documented and has OpenAPI specs. However, you can only get a tenant or sandbox to build and test against through a Salesforce license (contact for pricing) or a partner realm. There is no free developer tier. Even with a tenant, each merchant has to provision its own Account Manager or SLAS client and share its tenant IDs, so there is no central OAuth app for multi-user connection. I could not confirm native outbound webhooks.

what: Ecommerce platform (Magento Open Source / Adobe Commerce) exposing per-store REST, GraphQL, and SOAP APIs.
mcpNotes: Adobe's own MCP tooling is the Commerce extensibility developer agent: an App Builder MCP server plus Dropins tools, meant for IDE and development work, not store operations. Third-party store-operations servers include CData, StackOne (hosted), Cequence AI Gateway, Truto, rafaelstz/adobe-commerce-dev-mcp, and Marketplace modules from miniOrange, Freento and Webdevs. No official Adobe MCP server for store operations was found.
blockerNotes: The API is per-merchant and self-hosted: each user must supply their store base URL and credentials, and there is no central OAuth app. On PaaS and Open Source the default integration auth is OAuth 1.0a request signing. Simple bearer use needs the merchant to enable a config flag. SaaS needs a separate Adobe IMS OAuth 2.0 path. Webhooks are synchronous and configured on the store side (Adobe Commerce Webhooks module), and the asynchronous I/O Events path needs App Builder.

what: Website builder with ecommerce; Commerce APIs for products, orders, inventory, contacts.
mcpNotes: I found no official Squarespace MCP server. Glama lists only third-party servers, for example The1Studio/squarespace-mcp and timncox/Squarespace MCP. Zapier, StackOne, Metorial and MCPBundles offer hosted connectors. A GitHub issue (anthropics/claude-ai-mcp#372) asks for an official connector.
blockerNotes: A multi-tenant toolkit needs an OAuth client, which Squarespace must review and approve before it issues any credentials. The approved client also has to be tied to an Extension. Without approval, the only option is a per-site API key on the paid Commerce Advanced plan. The API covers commerce only, not site content or design.

what: Lightspeed-owned hosted ecommerce platform that embeds online stores in any site.
mcpNotes: I found no official Ecwid or Lightspeed MCP server for the store API. The GitBook docs site has a docs-search MCP endpoint at docs.ecwid.com/~gitbook/mcp, but it only searches documentation and is not an API server. Third-party MCP servers exist from Zapier (zapier.com/mcp/ecwid), viaSocket, Truto, Jentic, Unified.to and Mushrooms.
blockerNotes: A toolkit acting for many merchants needs a public OAuth app. That means App Market review (1-2 business days, with every update re-approved) and a partner contract with revenue share. Development works on a test store after emailing support for a free paid-plan upgrade. Only paid-plan merchants can use the API.

what: Platform for creators to sell digital products, memberships and courses directly to customers.
mcpNotes: Gumroad hosts its own MCP server at https://gumroad.com/claude/v1/mcp, with OAuth sign-in. gumroad.com/mcp lists a separate URL for each assistant, and access is revoked from Gumroad settings. Community servers also exist, such as the npm package gumroad-mcp.
blockerNotes: Public REST API with self-serve OAuth apps and tokens, plus an official hosted MCP server. The API covers less than the full product: there are no endpoints for writing posts, emails or payouts. I found no documented test mode.

what: REST API for Amazon sellers' and vendors' orders, listings, inventory, fulfillment, reports and finances.
mcpNotes: Amazon's own repo, amzn/selling-partner-api-samples, holds two local MCP servers. The first is sp-api-dev-mcp, published on npm as @amazon-sp-api-release/sp-api-dev-mcp, which bundles a Developer Assistant and a Workflow builder. The second is amazon-data-kiosk-mcp-server, which queries the Data Kiosk API. Both run locally with your own LWA credentials. There is no vendor-hosted remote MCP. Many community servers also exist.
blockerNotes: Developer registration and role approval are required before you get credentials. A public multi-seller OAuth app needs an Appstore listing and Amazon's review, and PII and other restricted roles need extra approval. Private self-authorized use is limited to the developer's own Professional seller account. The paid-fee blocker announced for 2026 was withdrawn in May 2026.

what: Creator/info-product checkout and payments platform (FanBasis, rebranded Commas) with REST API.
mcpNotes: The vendor's own MCP server is in beta. The commas.com homepage lists "MCP (beta): Run Commas from your AI assistant", covering checkout links, refunds and reporting. Per the indexed commasdocs.com text, the remote URL is https://www.fanbasis.com/mcp and it authenticates with a FanBasis API key. A one-click Claude Desktop install also exists. Zapier separately lists a FanBasis MCP integration, which is third-party.
blockerNotes: The API key is per merchant, with no OAuth, so each user must supply their own key. The product was renamed: FanBasis became Commas on 2026-07-14, but the API host is still fanbasis.com. Pricing is quote-based, and live-payment onboarding is unverified. The docs site (commasdocs.com) is a JavaScript SPA that automated fetching could not render, so the endpoint details rest on indexed text.

what: Pay-as-you-go APIs for SEO data: SERP, keywords, backlinks, on-page, and business data.
mcpNotes: The remote endpoint is https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp, which the vendor calls its "official DataForSEO remote endpoint". It uses OAuth 2.0 by default. Repo: github.com/dataforseo/mcp-server-typescript. The npm package dataforseo-mcp-server runs locally. The vendor page also describes an "official DataForSEO MCP image" for Docker.
blockerNotes: Users need their own DataForSEO account. Live data needs a funded balance (minimum top-up $50, after a $1 trial credit). Because the REST API uses Basic auth, each user enters credentials instead of going through an OAuth flow. Development and testing can run free against the Sandbox.

what: SEO platform with APIs for keyword, backlink, SERP, audit and rank-tracking data.
mcpNotes: Hosted at https://api.seranking.com/mcp (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, or the X-Api-Key header). Docs are at seranking.com/api/integrations/mcp/. The vendor's GitHub org also publishes a self-hostable server, github.com/seranking/seo-data-api-mcp-server, which uses the SERANKING_API_TOKEN env var.
blockerNotes: A developer can test on the 14-day free trial (no card needed). Lasting use needs a paid subscription, and Data API calls consume credits. The REST API offers only full-access API keys, with no third-party OAuth app flow, so users must paste their own keys.

what: SEO data platform: backlinks, keywords, SERPs, rank tracking, site audit, via API.
mcpNotes: Official hosted MCP server at https://api.ahrefs.com/mcp/mcp (Streamable HTTP). It uses an OAuth consent screen, and you can also generate an MCP key manually. It is for Lite plans and higher. I did not re-check the first pass's claim that the old local repo is archived.
blockerNotes: Building is self-serve: Connect needs no plan, and inactive apps get free test requests. Shipping public OAuth to other users needs Ahrefs approval, and per the help center the app needs Lite or higher to activate. End users need paid Ahrefs plans and spend their own API units on every call (50-unit minimum per paid request). Tokens expire after a year with no refresh, so users must periodically re-authorize.

what: AI web scraping platform with a scraper API, web search, and scraper workflows.
mcpNotes: The hosted server is at https://mcp.mrscraper.com/mcp and uses OAuth 2.1, with an API key accepted as a bearer token as a fallback. The local option is the npm package @mrscraper/mcp (v0.6.1), run with npx over stdio. It has 7 tools: status, scrapeHtml, scrapeMarkdown, getScreenshot, scrapeBrand, scrapeJson, and webSearch.
blockerNotes: API tokens are self-serve, but there is no ongoing free tier. The only free access is a 7-day trial that needs a card and auto-bills ($99/mo Essential). The API is narrow, and an official MCP server already covers most of it. Webhooks exist per scraper for the started, completed, and failed events. They are set up in the dashboard, not through the API, and no signature verification is documented.

what: Cloud platform for running web scraping and automation Actors, with storage for their results.
mcpNotes: Hosted at https://mcp.apify.com. OAuth is recommended; an 'Authorization: Bearer <APIFY_TOKEN>' header also works. Apify also publishes a local npm package, @apify/actors-mcp-server (GitHub apify/apify-mcp-server).
blockerNotes: Personal or scoped API tokens are self-serve on the free plan, which is enough to build now. OAuth 2.0 for integrations exists, but registration is not publicly documented; you would likely need to contact integrations@apify.com for a client ID and secret. Rate limits are generous: 250k requests/min globally and 60 requests/s per resource by default.

what: Web search, scrape, crawl and browser-interaction API that returns LLM-ready Markdown/JSON.
mcpNotes: Vendor-hosted servers: https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (API key as a bearer token, or keyless for search, scrape and parse) and https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth (OAuth browser sign-in). The docs also link a guide to run the server locally (firecrawl-mcp).
blockerNotes: API keys are self-serve on a free tier, and there is a published OpenAPI spec. The only friction is the low free-plan rate limits (2 to 10 requests per minute) and credit-based metering, with each user needing their own key.

what: Web data platform: proxies, Web Unlocker, SERP API, scrapers, datasets, cloud browsers.
mcpNotes: The hosted server is https://mcp.brightdata.com/mcp?token=YOUR_API_TOKEN_HERE. The local server is the npm package @brightdata/mcp (GitHub repo brightdata/brightdata-mcp). It exposes 31 tools.
blockerNotes: Nothing blocks a build. Each user brings an API key because there is no OAuth, and usage is billed to that user's account. Webhooks are per-job delivery callbacks: Bright Data POSTs results to an endpoint you set on the trigger, with an optional auth_header. They are not account-level event subscriptions.

what: Open-source CLI that checks a username across 400+ social networks to find accounts.
mcpNotes: There is no official MCP server from sherlock-project. The relevant community wrapper is Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp, a FastMCP stdio server with one search_username tool that shells out to the Sherlock CLI. Several servers share the name but are unrelated: H4RR1SON/covertlabs "Sherlock MCP" is for Covertlabs infostealer intelligence, and Fewsats/sherlock-mcp on PyPI is for buying domains.
blockerNotes: Sherlock is a local CLI with no hosted API or auth. A toolkit would have to run the CLI (or Docker image) on infrastructure Composio hosts. The other option is a third-party Apify actor, which is a separate product with its own billing.

what: B2B contact and company search and enrichment API that queries several data providers in sequence.
mcpNotes: I found no official Waterfall.io MCP server in the docs, in llms.txt or in a web search. Waterfall publishes agent 'skills' instead, waterfall-direct-api and waterfall-integration, in a GitHub repository. These are not MCP servers. Workato's 'Waterfall Lead Enrichment MCP server' is a different product that chains ZoomInfo, Apollo and LeadIQ, so it does not count.
blockerNotes: Getting a key requires vendor approval, and use is billed under a contract with credit-based pricing and minimums. The toolkit itself is simple (REST plus API key, with an OpenAPI spec), but Composio and every end user need an approved key, and there is no free or test tier for development.

what: GTM data enrichment and prospecting platform: find people and companies, then enrich them.
mcpNotes: Clay hosts an official MCP at https://api.clay.com/v3/mcp, confirmed on Clay University's "Connect to Clay MCP" page. It uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and DCR, and runs Clay's find-and-enrich tools and custom functions on behalf of a signed-in user. Workspace admins gate which clients are allowed. Clay also ships a local stdio `clay mcp` with its CLI and agent plugin, which authenticates through `clay login`. Neither MCP accepts an API key.
blockerNotes: The API is self-serve on all plans, but it is narrow (about 18 operations) and new, focused on routines and searches. Table queries are Enterprise-only. Every call consumes credits. The Public API is API-key only. An OAuth path exists through the hosted MCP, but each workspace admin must allow the client. Webhooks fire when a routine run finishes.

what: Code hosting and collaboration platform: repos, issues, PRs, Actions CI.
mcpNotes: Remote server at https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/, hosted by GitHub, with OAuth or PAT auth. Source is open at github.com/github/github-mcp-server, which can also be run locally.
blockerNotes: No blocker. GitHub Apps and OAuth apps are self-serve and free. Org owners may need to approve or install the app. There is no separate sandbox environment, but a free test account or org works as one.

what: Cloud platform for deploying and hosting web apps, with domains, functions and storage.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.vercel.com is Vercel's official remote MCP server, using OAuth and Streamable HTTP. It is available on all plans. Clients must use a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) or be reviewed and approved by Vercel. The docs have moved to https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp.
blockerNotes: The REST API is broad and has an OpenAPI spec. Credentials are self-serve: free Hobby accounts can create personal tokens, and Integrations can be self-created and installed by external users with a Community badge. Caveats: long-lived integration tokens are deprecated, so a toolkit should use short-lived client_credentials tokens per installation. Sign in with Vercel's API permissions are in private beta. Account webhooks and the billing scope need Pro or Enterprise. A public marketplace listing needs 500 installs and a review. There is no separate test mode, but a free Hobby account works for testing.

what: Web hosting, serverless functions and deploy platform for web projects.
mcpNotes: Remote: https://mcp.netlify.com/mcp. The old URL, https://netlify-mcp.netlify.app/mcp, still works. Local package: @netlify/mcp. Repo: github.com/netlify/netlify-mcp. Users sign in through a login link; the docs give no PAT or OAuth details for the remote server.
blockerNotes: Public REST API with self-serve OAuth2 app registration and an OpenAPI spec, available on the free plan. Outgoing webhooks (hooks API) cover a limited set of events, e.g. submission_created, deploy_created, deploy_failed. Deploy rate limits are strict (3/min, 100/day).

what: Edge network, CDN, DNS, security, Workers serverless and developer platform.
mcpNotes: The main server is https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. It provides search() and execute() tools across the whole API, plus docs(). It authenticates with OAuth, or with an API token sent as a bearer token. Optional product servers are docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, containers.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, browser.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, dex.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, casb.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp and agents.cloudflare.com/mcp.
blockerNotes: There is no real blocker. A public OAuth client needs only domain verification (a DNS TXT record), not a manual review. Webhooks are limited to Notifications alert delivery; there are no general resource-change event subscriptions. There is no separate sandbox, but a free account works as a test environment.

what: Postgres backend platform: database, auth, storage, edge functions, plus a Management API.
mcpNotes: The hosted server is at https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp, with an open-source repo at github.com/supabase/mcp. By default it uses OAuth with dynamic client registration; a PAT in the Authorization header is available for CI, and clients that need it can use an OAuth client ID and secret.
blockerNotes: Credentials are self-serve on the free tier: PATs and OAuth apps created in the dashboard, with no documented review step. The OpenAPI spec is published. Caveats: (1) Platform Webhooks (/v2/.../webhooks/endpoints) are early access, allowlisted orgs only, and others get 403 access_disabled, which limits trigger support. (2) OAuth app "publishing" isn't explained in the docs. (3) An official hosted MCP server exists, so a toolkit would overlap with it.

what: Graph database; Aura API manages cloud instances, Query API runs Cypher over HTTP.
mcpNotes: The official Neo4j MCP server lives at github.com/neo4j/mcp (releases). It installs with `uvx neo4j-mcp-server` from PyPI or `brew install neo4j-mcp`, and also ships as a binary and as the Docker image mcp/neo4j. It runs over stdio (default) or HTTP, and connects to one Neo4j database to do schema exploration and Cypher. I found no vendor-hosted remote URL. Separately, the neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j servers, including an Aura manager, are Labs/community projects.
blockerNotes: There is no multi-user OAuth consent flow, so each user has to paste in an Aura client ID and secret (client_credentials). For data access, each user also has to supply a database URI plus a username and password or an SSO token. Rate limits on the free tier are low (25 requests per minute). The official OpenAPI spec could not be downloaded (api.neo4j.io/openapi.json returned 403), and no webhooks are documented.

what: Cloud data platform for SQL analytics, data engineering, and AI workloads.
mcpNotes: The Snowflake-managed MCP server is at https://<account_url>/api/v2/databases/{database}/schemas/{schema}/mcp-servers/{name}. It accepts OAuth (Snowflake OAuth by default, or External OAuth) or a PAT as a Bearer token. The docs don't say whether it is GA or preview.
blockerNotes: Each account has its own hostname, so the toolkit must collect the account identifier for each user. OAuth needs an admin to create a security integration. PATs need a network policy by default. Free use is limited to a 30-day, credit-capped trial, with AI features gated behind adding a card. There is no event-subscription webhook API. Snowflake's own notification integrations and alerts only send messages a customer defines, so triggers would need polling.

what: Managed cloud MongoDB service; the Admin API manages orgs, projects, clusters and users.
mcpNotes: The Atlas Managed MCP Server is hosted by MongoDB at https://mcp.mongodb.com. It went GA on 2026-08-13, uses OAuth through Atlas App Connections, and is disabled by default for existing orgs. There is also an official local server, the npm package mongodb-mcp-server (github.com/mongodb-js/mongodb-mcp-server). It uses MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_ID and MDB_MCP_API_CLIENT_SECRET for Atlas tools and supports stdio or HTTP transport.
blockerNotes: A toolkit can be built today with service account credentials (OAuth client credentials) that each customer supplies. The catch is that customers must create a service account themselves and either add the toolkit's egress IPs to the API access list or disable the list. A real per-user OAuth connect flow needs MongoDB to approve you as a design partner (via the Become a Partner form, mentioning "Partner API"). Each customer org must also enable third-party app connections, which are off by default for existing orgs. There is no separate partner or test environment. Webhooks only deliver alert notifications per project; there is no general event subscription.

what: Cloud observability platform: metrics, logs, traces, monitors, dashboards, incidents, security.
mcpNotes: The Datadog-hosted MCP server has per-site endpoints, for example https://mcp.datadoghq.com/v1/mcp and https://mcp.datadoghq.eu/v1/mcp, with US3/US5/AP1/AP2/UK1 variants. US1-FED and US2-FED are not supported. Auth options are OAuth 2.0 (recommended), PAT/SAT as a Bearer token, or API plus app key headers. The docs say it is "under significant development", and some toolsets are in Preview.
blockerNotes: A toolkit can be built today with per-user API and app keys or PATs, which any org can create, including Free-tier orgs. The user's site has to be captured too. A published, public OAuth integration requires Datadog Partner Network membership and a partner developer org, and the client works only inside that org until Datadog publishes it. OAuth clients also get only a limited scope set.

what: Application error monitoring, tracing, session replay and alerting platform.
mcpNotes: Vendor-hosted remote server at https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp, which uses OAuth for all connections. A stdio option runs through the Sentry CLI (`sentry mcp`), and the legacy `npx @sentry/mcp-server` package also exists. The pricing page lists 'MCP access' on the free Developer plan.
blockerNotes: A multi-tenant OAuth toolkit needs a published public integration, and publishing means Sentry reviews it (the Publish button emails integrations-platform@sentry.io). Until it is approved, an unpublished integration is only for development. Also, the pricing page says the free Developer plan has no API access, so end users on the free tier may not be able to use the toolkit. Tokens are scoped to one organization.

what: All-in-one workspace for notes, docs, databases, wikis and project management.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp, hosted by Notion. It uses OAuth by default. MCP bearer tokens are available on Business and Enterprise only, and only workspace owners can create them. Business and Enterprise also get higher MCP rate limits.
blockerNotes: Public OAuth connections work without Marketplace review. On Free and Plus, only workspace owners can create the connection. End users must pick which pages the integration can access. There is no dedicated sandbox, but a free workspace can be used for testing.

what: Spreadsheet-database platform for building collaborative apps, workflows and tables.
mcpNotes: Airtable hosts an official MCP server at https://mcp.airtable.com/mcp. It authenticates with OAuth or a PAT and is available on all plans (support article "Using the Airtable MCP server"). Community servers also exist, such as domdomegg/airtable-mcp-server.
blockerNotes: There is no blocker for building. Users on the Free plan are capped at 1,000 API calls per workspace per month, which limits heavy agent use. Webhooks created with PAT or OAuth tokens expire after 7 days unless refreshed or their payloads are listed. Webhook notifications are pings containing only the base and webhook IDs, so payloads must be fetched separately. Airtable publishes no official OpenAPI spec. There is no dedicated sandbox, so a free account serves as the dev environment.

what: Issue tracking and project management for software teams, with cycles, projects and roadmaps.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.linear.app/mcp is read-write and https://mcp.linear.app/mcp/readonly is read-only. Transport is Streamable HTTP; the /sse endpoint is a deprecated fallback. The interactive flow uses OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. The server also accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` with an OAuth token or an API key.
blockerNotes: There is no review gate for OAuth apps, and API and webhooks are included on the Free plan. The API is GraphQL only, so there is no OpenAPI spec. Linear has no dedicated sandbox, but a free workspace (250-issue cap) can serve as a test environment. Rate limits are 2,500 req/h for API keys and 5,000 req/h for OAuth apps, plus complexity-point limits.

what: Issue and project tracking for teams, with broad REST and GraphQL APIs.
mcpNotes: The Atlassian Rovo MCP server is at https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp. It uses OAuth 2.1, with API token auth as an option. It covers Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Bitbucket and more. Some enriched calls consume Rovo credits.
blockerNotes: There are minor caveats. Review of OAuth apps is optional, but users installing an unreviewed app see a warning. Webhooks registered through the REST API expire after 30 days unless refreshed. OAuth 2.0 apps are limited to 5 webhooks per app per user on a tenant.

what: Work and project management platform for tasks, projects, and team collaboration.
mcpNotes: The official remote server is at https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp. It uses Streamable HTTP and OAuth. Some clients need a client ID and secret from an Asana app. The v1 beta server at https://mcp.asana.com/sse was deprecated and was scheduled to shut down on 2026-05-11. Admin controls for allowing or blocking MCP clients exist only on Enterprise+ and Legacy Enterprise tiers.
blockerNotes: No blocker found. OAuth apps are self-serve and can be shared with 'Any workspace' without review. Review applies only to App Directory listing. Service accounts and some premium features depend on the plan. Workspace admins may block third-party apps.

what: Work management platform for boards, items, and workflows across teams.
mcpNotes: The vendor hosts a Platform MCP at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp. It uses Streamable HTTP, according to search summaries; SSE is deprecated. You can authenticate with an API token, your own OAuth app, or dynamic client registration. There is also an open-source local package, @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp (github.com/mondaycom/mcp).
blockerNotes: Nothing blocks a build. The public GraphQL API, free developer tokens and OAuth are all available. OAuth apps can be shared without marketplace review, but they show an "unvetted" banner. The Free plan's limit of 200 calls a day could restrict end users on free accounts.

what: Work management platform for tasks, docs, goals and team collaboration.
mcpNotes: The URL is https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp. It supports OAuth only; personal API keys and OAuth access tokens are not accepted. It is available on all plans. The current docs page no longer says it is in beta.
blockerNotes: No blockers found. OAuth apps are self-serve and have no documented review. Limits on lower plans are 100 req/min per token, which is modest but workable.

what: Collaborative docs-plus-tables workspace (Coda, now Superhuman Docs) with automations and Packs.
mcpNotes: The vendor hosts the official Superhuman Docs (formerly Coda) MCP server. It is in public beta and connects through OAuth ("Connect with Superhuman Docs") or a personal MCP token. The endpoint https://docs.superhuman.com/apis/mcp comes from a search summary; I did not see it on a vendor page. The vendor's tool list is at coda.io/resources/mcp/tools-and-endpoints. Paid plans include the MCP; free plans get read-only access with a cap. I could not verify the first pass's claims of about 15 tools and a deprecation of the old Coda MCP. Community servers exist, e.g. the PyPI package mcp-coda.
blockerNotes: Buildable today with free, self-serve per-user API tokens against a broad REST API that has an OpenAPI spec. Caveats: the REST API has no third-party OAuth, so users must paste tokens. Webhooks only go inbound: POST /docs/{docId}/hooks/automation/{ruleId} triggers an automation, and the spec has no outbound event subscriptions, so triggers would need polling. The product was rebranded from Coda to Superhuman Docs; the docs moved to docs.superhuman.com, but API hosts stay on coda.io.

what: Work management platform with sheets, projects, automation, reports and dashboards.
mcpNotes: Official hosted MCP server at https://mcp.smartsheet.com (US), https://mcp.smartsheet.eu (EU) and https://mcp.smartsheet.au (AU). It went GA on March 24, 2026, authenticates with OAuth 2.0 or a personal access token, and needs a Business, Enterprise or AWM plan. The older local repo, smartsheet-platform/smar-mcp on GitHub, is deprecated in favour of the hosted server.
blockerNotes: Getting an API token, registering an OAuth app in Developer Tools and using the MCP server all need a licensed Business-or-higher account. No free sandbox exists. Once you have a paid seat, OAuth app registration is self-serve with no documented review.

what: Time tracking, invoicing and expense SaaS with a public REST API v2.
mcpNotes: Harvest's support article "Harvest MCP" gives the endpoint https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp. It is added as a custom connector in Claude, or in Claude Code with `claude mcp add --transport http harvest https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp`, and the article has setup steps for Cursor. Fetching the article directly returns 403, so this comes from search snippets of Harvest's own page. Its auth (probably OAuth) is not confirmed. Community servers also exist: ianaleck/harvest-mcp-server, taiste, standardbeagle, valtirallc and southleft.
blockerNotes: No blocker found. OAuth2 apps and PATs are self-serve with no documented review, and a Free plan exists. The rate limits are modest, especially on Reports (100 requests per 15 minutes). There are no native webhooks, so triggers would have to poll.

what: Payments, billing, invoicing, payouts and financial infrastructure platform with a broad REST API.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.stripe.com (official, remote). Supports OAuth (refresh tokens expire after 14 days) or agent API keys sent as a Bearer token. Tools include stripe_api_search, stripe_api_details, stripe_api_read, stripe_api_write, get_stripe_account_info, stripe_analytics, Treasury tools and search_stripe_documentation. From 11 January 2027 it will reject full-access secret keys and non-agent restricted keys. OAuth isn't supported when acting on connected accounts; use an agent key with the Stripe-Account header instead.
blockerNotes: Per-user OAuth for public distribution needs a public Stripe App, which requires an activated account and passing Marketplace app review (about 4 business days, with re-review on changes). Connect OAuth is not a clean alternative because Stripe calls it deprecated. API keys (preferably restricted or agent keys) work immediately with no review, so an API-key toolkit can ship today.

what: Financial data API linking bank accounts: transactions, balances, identity, payments, income.
mcpNotes: Dashboard MCP server: https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/ (Streamable HTTP, Bearer token from /oauth/token with the client_credentials grant and mcp:dashboard scope). It works with Production data only and requires Production approval. It covers Dashboard and diagnostic tasks, not end-user financial data. Plaid also offers a local MCP server in its AI coding toolkit, which provides mock data, docs search, Sandbox tokens, and webhook simulation.
blockerNotes: Sandbox is self-serve. Live bank data requires Production enablement by Plaid. Some bank APIs also need the security questionnaire and institution registration. Each end user must link accounts through Plaid Link. Credentials are per developer team, and there is no third-party OAuth, so a multi-tenant toolkit would need customers to supply their own client_id and secret plus Item access_tokens.

what: Global crypto exchange with spot, futures, margin, wallet and trading APIs.
mcpNotes: Binance hosts an official MCP server at https://agent.binance.com/mcp/agentic, part of Binance Agent OS. It covers market data, plus trading in Spot, Margin, Convert, USDⓈ-M and COIN-M Futures inside a dedicated Agentic sub-account. It authenticates through a browser consent flow, stores no local API keys and has no withdrawal scope. The Binance Skills Hub is also official. Community servers such as the PyPI binance-mcp-server also exist.
blockerNotes: The API is buildable with per-user API keys. Each end user needs a KYC-verified, funded Binance account in a supported region and must paste in a key and secret, often with an IP whitelist. OAuth is partner-only, so there is no standard delegated-auth flow. Rate limits are per IP, so users would share one limit behind a shared backend. Trading actions are high-risk.

what: NMI-powered white-label payment gateway; the "Paygent Connect" branding is unverified.
mcpNotes: No MCP server for Paygent was found. NMI hosts a docs MCP server, listed on docs.nmi.com/reference, that lets AI coding assistants query NMI's documentation. It does not call the payments API, and it belongs to NMI, not Paygent. An unrelated "Paygent" MCP connector (ai.paygenthq, on Glama) exists for an AI-agent payments product and should not be confused with this one.
blockerNotes: The product identity is the main blocker. "Paygent" is the name of at least four unrelated companies: Japan's Paygent (connect ID/password credentials), gopaygent.com (an API-first gateway that markets a "Connect" marketplace product), pay-gent.com, and paygent.tech/paygenthq (AI-agent payments with MCP). No source ties any of them to NMI. If the product really is an NMI white-label, a toolkit could target the NMI API with per-merchant security keys. Production accounts come only through NMI partners.

what: FX audit API scoring bank/card FX rates against live mid-market rates, with MCP server.
mcpNotes: https://hvujzsdwcoweirroubeh.supabase.co/functions/v1/mcp-server. The transport appears to be Streamable HTTP (the example sends Accept: application/json, text/event-stream). Auth is Bearer with an ipx_ key. Documented at ipayx.ai/docs/mcp-server.
blockerNotes: The API has only 3 endpoints and the product is niche. According to the homepage, API access needs a paid plan (Credit Pack $99 or Unlimited $299/mo). Auth is a per-user API key with no OAuth. A test-key format (ipx_test_) appears only on the MCP docs page, and there is no documented sandbox environment.

what: Cloud accounting software for small businesses: invoicing, bills, payments, bookkeeping.
mcpNotes: Hosted: https://ai-inc.quickbooks.intuit.com/v1/mcp, on Intuit's domain, using Streamable HTTP and OAuth through Intuit sign-in. Directories credit it to QuickBooks, and it is reportedly listed in Claude's directory as 'Made by Intuit QuickBooks'. Local: github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server, MIT licence, stdio, 145 tools. Many third-party hosted servers also exist.
blockerNotes: Development and sandbox work is self-serve. Connecting real companies needs production keys gated by the per-app assessment questionnaire, plus terms, company address and other setup. Read-heavy agent usage may exceed the free Builder cap of 500k CorePlus calls per month, which needs a paid tier.

what: Cloud accounting software for small businesses: invoicing, bank feeds, payroll, reporting.
mcpNotes: Xero hosts an official Developer Remote MCP at https://api.xero.com/mcp/v1. It authenticates with OAuth 2.0 plus PKCE, reads and writes Xero data, and is included on Core and above (Starter apps get the demo organisation only). Xero also publishes a local server, XeroAPI/xero-mcp-server (MIT, npm @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server, 51 tools), which authenticates with either a Custom Connection or a bearer token. A directory lists a separate endpoint, mcp.xero.com/mcp, but I could not confirm it on Xero's own site.
blockerNotes: Building and testing are free on Starter, but Starter caps an app at 5 connected organisations and 1,000 calls per day per organisation. Serving many end users needs Core (A$35/mo, 50 connections) or higher. That means a credit card, egress billing (A$2.40/GB over the allotment), and, at higher tiers, App Certification and an annual Security Assessment. Core and above allow 5,000 calls per day per organisation. Some premium endpoints (Journals, XPM, Bulk Connections) need extra approval.

what: Corporate cards, spend management, expenses, bill pay and business banking platform.
mcpNotes: https://api.brex.com/mcp (Beta). Uses OAuth with DCR. An account or card admin must accept the Developer API agreement and enable the "Brex in AI assistants" beta under Settings → Beta features.
blockerNotes: A multi-user OAuth toolkit needs partner client credentials from Brex developer support. Fallback: each customer pastes an admin-created user token, which works on the free Essentials plan but only for Brex customers. The staging sandbox is only for partners, has no availability guarantees and may be purged. The customer API is production-only. The official MCP (OAuth + DCR) is beta and must be enabled per company.

what: Corporate cards, spend management, bill pay and accounting automation for businesses.
mcpNotes: The hosted Ramp MCP is at https://mcp.ramp.com/mcp and is documented on docs.ramp.com. Users sign in with Ramp OAuth and act as themselves with Full access or Read-only. Connections expire after 30 days. Custom clients need their redirect URI allowlisted by Ramp, which is done by request. The older local package, github.com/ramp-public/ramp_mcp (client credentials, demo or prod), was archived on 2026-07-17. Third-party directories also list a developer-docs MCP and a Ramp Data MCP (API key) under mcp.ramp.com, but I didn't verify those in Ramp's docs.
blockerNotes: A multi-customer OAuth integration needs Ramp's technology partnership application, security disclosures, SSO and a review of integration flows before production access ("Approval is required before production access"). The sandbox is also by request. A single customer can still use Client Credentials for their own business without this. Inside each customer, an Admin must approve the app.

what: Private-market data on companies, deals, investors, funds and LPs, via a contract-gated API.
mcpNotes: The official server is https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp ("PitchBook Premium"). Claude's marketplace lists it as made by PitchBook. PitchBook help pages describe it as the Premium Connector for Claude, and there is also a ChatGPT version. To use it you need a seat-based, unlimited or trial PitchBook license plus SSO credentials, and a Claude org owner must enable it first. PitchBook currently includes it free for subscribers. Third-party wrappers exist from Strac, Apify, Merge and Vinkius.
blockerNotes: The API is public, documented and key-based, and Composio already ships a 130-tool PitchBook toolkit with API_KEY auth, so it can be built. The catch is that each end-user organization must hold a PitchBook subscription plus a separately contracted API add-on with credits. Composio cannot get test credentials without a contract or partnership. The official remote MCP is an alternative for PitchBook license holders.

what: Google's AI research notebook; Enterprise edition exposes a preview notebooks API.
mcpNotes: NotebookLM is not on Google's managed MCP "Supported products" page (docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/supported-products). The page lists an Agent Search MCP at discoveryengine.googleapis.com/mcp, which is a different product. Only community servers exist, e.g. pleaseprompto/notebooklm-mcp, PyPI notebooklm-mcp-server, mcp-notebooklm and moodrobotics/notebooklm-mcp-server. They are unofficial and mostly automate the consumer web app using cookies or browser sessions.
blockerNotes: End users need a paid Gemini Notebook/Gemini Enterprise license on a Google Cloud project; a developer can build and test on the 14-day trial. The API is v1alpha/Pre-GA. The surface covers notebook, source and audio-overview management, with no chat/query. Auth is user OAuth with cloud-platform scope, so a public OAuth app would likely face Google sensitive-scope verification. Consumer NotebookLM has no API.

what: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp uses Streamable HTTP and OAuth and has three read-only tools: get_user_info, search and fetch. Claude's connector directory lists it as "Made by Otter.ai" and Anthropic-verified. It is also listed as an OpenAI ChatGPT plugin. Otter's pricing page includes it on the Basic plan.
blockerNotes: A toolkit can be built today on the official MCP server: it uses OAuth, works on free accounts, and Composio already ships otter_ai_mcp. That server has only three read-only tools (search, fetch, user info).
