Fuller REST access and webhook triggers need an Enterprise plan (custom pricing, schedule a demo) and per-user static Bearer keys.

what: AI meeting recorder that transcribes, summarizes, and shares call notes.
mcpNotes: Fathom hosts an MCP server at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp, documented at developers.fathom.ai/mcp-docs with ChatGPT and Claude guides. The pricing page lists MCP under Team/Premium and says "Only for work domains; Max 5 users / domain".
blockerNotes: Credentials are self-serve on all plans, and OAuth app registration is a form. The main limit is the small API: 11 mostly read-only operations covering meetings, recordings, teams, users, and webhooks, with no write actions on meetings or notes. Rate limits are tight (60/min, and 30/min for transcripts and summaries). Fathom may review OAuth apps, but the docs don't say review blocks installs.

what: AI search engine over peer-reviewed papers, with a cited-answer research agent.
mcpNotes: The hosted server is at https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp and supports OAuth sign-in or a Bearer API key. The repo is github.com/Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp and the setup guide is at docs.consensus.app/consensus-mcp. The MCP search tool works without an account, and a free tier allows 30 calls a month.
blockerNotes: REST access needs a paid plan, and one Consensus page says Team access is "available upon approval". The API surface is small. The OAuth the request asked for is available only on the MCP server, not the REST API. A toolkit could use REST with each user's own API key, or wrap the official remote MCP over OAuth, which also covers free and no-account users with limits. The docs site (docs.consensus.app) returns 403 to automated fetches.

what: API for parsing, extracting, splitting, classifying and editing documents into structured data.
mcpNotes: Reducto hosts it at https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp and documents it at docs.reducto.ai/mcp-server. Auth is the API key as Authorization: Bearer. I opened the page directly and confirmed these details.
blockerNotes: The API is public, self-serve and comes with $150 of free credit. Auth uses a user-supplied API key rather than OAuth. The API is narrow in purpose (document processing) but has a reasonable number of operations.

what: Autonomous AI software engineer from Cognition, controllable via REST API and MCP.
mcpNotes: https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP; legacy SSE is deprecated). It needs a `cog_` Devin API key as Bearer; enterprise keys and PATs also need X-Org-Id. Tools cover wiki (read_wiki_structure, ask_wiki_question, etc.), devin_session_create/search/interact/events/gather, playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations, MCP server management, automations, reviews, code scans and user list. A separate no-auth DeepWiki MCP is at https://mcp.deepwiki.com/.
blockerNotes: Each customer has to create a service-user key or PAT in their own Teams/Enterprise org. There is no OAuth for multi-user distribution, and the Enterprise API is enterprise only. There are no outbound webhooks: the docs' "webhook" use case has the customer's ticketing system call the Devin API, so triggers would need polling of session events.

what: AI image and video generation platform with a REST API, CLI and hosted MCP.
mcpNotes: Official hosted MCP at https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp. It uses OAuth 2.0 through Clerk (higgsfield.ai/_clerk) with PKCE and dynamic client registration, and no API key is needed. The official CLI is @higgsfield/cli (`npm i -g @higgsfield/cli`), which works with MCP-compatible CLI agents. A community wrapper also exists (geopopos/higgsfield_ai_mcp).
blockerNotes: This is not a hard blocker. The REST API has no per-user OAuth, so each user supplies their own key ID and secret, and usage needs a prepaid balance (minimum $5). The official hosted MCP already offers OAuth with dynamic client registration, which overlaps with a Composio toolkit.

what: Open-source CLI and Node library that renders Mermaid diagram text to SVG, PNG or PDF.
mcpNotes: The mermaid-js GitHub org has 14 repos and none of them is an MCP server. Community servers wrap or reimplement rendering: @peng-shawn/mermaid-mcp-server, mcp-mermaid (hustcc) and mermaid-render-mcp, which uses @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli. Separately, Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai), the commercial company behind Mermaid, runs an official remote MCP at https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp and /sse. It has 9 tools for validation, rendering and project/diagram CRUD, and needs a Mermaid account. The Stacklok "Official" listing points to that server's docs. It belongs to the Mermaid Chart product, not to mermaid-cli.
blockerNotes: This is a local CLI with no hosted API or user accounts. Composio could only self-host the renderer (headless Chromium via Puppeteer) as a utility, which would not be an authenticated integration. If the goal is "Mermaid" as a service, the buildable target is Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai): it has an official remote MCP with OAuth 2.1 and a free Basic tier. That is a different product from this hint.

what: Hosted REST API and MCP server for YouTube transcripts, search, channel and playlist data.
mcpNotes: The vendor hosts the server at https://transcriptapi.com/mcp. It takes OAuth 2.1 (Claude, ChatGPT) or an API key sent as a Bearer token, and exposes 12 tools, including get_youtube_transcript and search_youtube.
blockerNotes: The API is small, read-only and billed per credit. The 100 free credits cover development. A public OpenAPI 3.1 spec is published at /openapi.json.

what: AI meeting recorder that transcribes, summarizes, clips and shares meeting recordings.
mcpNotes: Grain hosts an 'Official Grain MCP Server', documented at developers.grain.com/mcp and support.grain.com/en/articles/14811968. Per the support page, it uses OAuth and HTTPS, and developers can also connect with a PAT. Some tools need Business or Enterprise. The endpoint https://api.grain.com/_/mcp (Streamable HTTP) appears in directory listings (mcpservers.org, Merge, Agentman) and in search snippets of developers.grain.com. When I fetched the vendor page, the URL was not in the rendered text. Workspace-scope tokens are rejected by the MCP server.
blockerNotes: PATs are self-serve on every plan, including Free, so a toolkit can be built today. The caveat is multi-user OAuth: Grain issues the client ID and secret manually, though Client ID Metadata Document public clients can avoid that step. Workspace-scope OAuth is limited to clients Grain has verified.
